resolution.rationale: Upstream v2.7.0 (#760) stops advertising sessionCapabilities.subagents to clients that are not AIR and adds an initialize test for it (it.each, standard client and AIR) at the position of the goal opt-in initialize test, so d173ce8 conflicted in initialize.test.ts only. The adaptation 0baf53f (stacked on the exact tag) keeps both tests; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to d173ce8. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change publishGoalSessionInfo, goalSessionInfoUpdate, goal control or the goal capability, so the non-AIR ACP v1 _meta.goal opt-in keeps its contract. The goal tests and the initialize tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and initialize.test.ts. Upstream v2.7.0 changes the server's subagent capability advert (#760), its session failure ids (#767), the fast service tier (#327) and subagent history replay (#760), but not createAsyncTasks, CodexBackgroundTerminalTasks, AsyncTaskExtension, ClientCapabilities or the _meta["async-tasks"] initialize advert. 808ea06 replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; its tests pass on the integration.

8f65eb8 replays cleanly, but upstream v2.7.0 (#767) replaces the event handler's session failure epoch with SessionFailureIds, one counter per connection that every prompt's handler shares. The pre-prompt goal subscription still passed this.sessionFailureEpoch, which no longer exists: npm run typecheck failed, and at run time the first notice or failure of goal work set before the first prompt threw. The adaptation 1716ad5 passes this.sessionFailureIds like upstream's prompt subscription; every other line is unchanged, and the prompt subscription it mirrors is otherwise identical between v2.6.0 and v2.7.0 (the new router argument of #760 is inside the shared router factory). The hook reports of #767 reach it through the same event handler. A new test (a hook that blocks goal work set before the first prompt is reported as a typed AIR session failure) fails with the old argument.

Upstream v2.7.0 (#760) makes the scenario baseline strip sessionCapabilities.subagents from each recorded initialize response and documents it next to the baseline comment that 57fdf79 changes, and #767 changes the CodexEventHandler import next to the patch's SessionInstructions import. The adaptation 904a70d (stacked on the exact candidate at its replay point) keeps upstream's subagents removal with the patch's _meta.systemPrompt capability in the baseline and both notes in its comment; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to 57fdf79. Upstream v2.7.0 only adds configOptions to the destructuring of newSessionV2/resumeSessionV2 and does not change the systemPrompt conversion that the ACP v1 _meta.systemPrompt.append alias feeds. The session instruction, initialize and scenario tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, initialize.test.ts and tool-call-contract.test.ts. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change SessionIndex, SessionIndexService, SessionListSubscriptions, publishAirSessionMetadata or the archive delivery fence that the v2.6.0 adaptation 688db7e publishes in; #760 gates sessionCapabilities.subagents with the same isAirClient helper the neutral index uses, without touching the session index advert. 688db7e replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; its tests pass on the integration.

Upstream v2.7.0 (#760) adds an initialize test (sessionCapabilities.subagents only for AIR) at the position of 2662df6's hook review initialize tests. The adaptation a2b37d3 keeps both; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to 2662df6. Upstream's #767 reports hook runs that block or stop Codex from hook/completed notifications in the event handler, independently of the _codex/hooks/list and _codex/hooks/trust review, the review token and the dispatch gate, which v2.7.0 does not touch (no change to AcpAgentRouter, CodexAppServerClient, CodexHookReview, CodexHookTrust or AppServerRecovery). The recovery, initialize and client profile tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and src/CodexAcpClient.ts. Upstream v2.7.0 only drops the ServiceTier casts of the session config builders in CodexAcpClient (#327) and does not change authenticate and its finally block, the provider restart, goal control, steering, CodexAppServerClient, CodexHookReview or GoalExtension. The #767 hook reports only read hook/completed notifications. 85c9871 replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; the recovery tests pass on the integration.
The authenticated prior patch ledger transition retired this patch.

Upstream v2.7.0 (#327) drops the ServiceTier import and cast from SessionFork.ts and adds a serviceTier option to the session lifecycle v2 test client, next to b1084b7's Turn import and capabilitiesMeta option. The adaptation fdcc23c imports Model and Turn without ServiceTier and keeps both test options; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to b1084b7. Upstream's fork code (resolveForkTurnId, the fork metadata) is otherwise unchanged in v2.7.0, so the fork point resolution and the forkPoint metadata keep their contract. The fork point tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and its initialize test files. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change GitPatch, FileChangeReporter or ClientCapabilities, and its plan (#752) and subagent (#760) changes do not touch file change reports, so the ACP v1 _meta.diffPatch keeps the Git-relative patch of the AIR extension. c51a9ec replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; its tests pass on the integration.

Upstream v2.7.0 (#767) replaces the event handler's session failure epoch and per-handler notice counter with SessionFailureIds, one counter per connection shared by every prompt's handler, passed as the fourth constructor argument; 8aaab39 conflicted there, in the server's three handler constructions and in the test helper. 8aaab39 numbered client-neutral incidents with the incident counter of its connection-wide NeutralSessionFailureLedger, which upstream's counter now does for both typed forms with the same <epoch>:<n> ids. The adaptation 3f96716 takes SessionFailureIds next to the format (upstream's boolean flag still means air or none), allocates failure and notice ids from it in both forms, drops the ledger's unused incident counter and keeps its revision floor (a later handler can still re-send <turnId>:error). With #755 a retry warning carries the trimmed Codex additionalDetails as details; the neutral record follows the AIR lane's title and details rules as docs/air-extensions.md states, so the neutral retry test now expects them. With #767 a hook that blocks or stops Codex is a notice, which a neutral client without session.notices gets as a _meta.sessionFailure record with kind notice. A new test covers that; it and the other neutral tests fail when the typed lane is AIR-only, the later-prompt id test fails with per-handler ids, and the cross-handler revision test fails without the revision floor.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and its initialize and contract tests. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change AgentFileChangeReport, the collectTurnDiffs argument of the event handler or the composed AIR publication that the v2.6.0 adaptation 95fb2c8 keeps; #760 changes the standard subagent views but not the turn diffs, and the patch's test of files a native subagent changed during the root turn passes on the new contract. 95fb2c8 replays cleanly; its tests and upstream's session-metadata-writers test pass on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and its initialize tests. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change permissions/metadata.ts, permissions/mcp.ts, CodexAsyncQuestions, CodexElicitationHandler or ClientCapabilities, so the ACP v1 _meta.permissionPresentation and the question custom answers keep their contract. 295ebe1 replays cleanly; the approval, elicitation and initialize tests pass on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and its initialize tests. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change ModelConfigOption or permissions/metadata.ts; #327 only lets the fast mode toggle treat Codex's canonical priority tier as fast, and #760 makes newSessionV2/resumeSessionV2 ignore initial config option values on ACP v2, neither of which touches the model and reasoning effort selectors or their ACP v1 recommendation records. ebc3010 replays cleanly; the session config option tests pass on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and its initialize tests. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change CodexCommands, buildAvailableCommands or the skill commands that the ACP v1 _meta.commandPresentation extends. ab965a0 replays cleanly; its tests pass on the integration.

Overlap only through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and its initialize tests. Upstream v2.7.0 does not change PromptSuggestionGenerator, the thread/sample request of CodexAppServerClient that it uses on an ephemeral fork of the session's thread, the v2 prompt harness or ClientCapabilities; its user message refactor (#760, userMessageContent) only changes how the adapter renders history to the client. 62ee6fe replays cleanly; the prompt suggestion tests pass on the integration.

Upstream v2.7.0 (#756) only bumps the pinned amannn/action-semantic-pull-request in conventional-prs.yml from v6.1.1 (48f256284bd4) to v6.1.2 (2252a14e810a). alas still pins v6.1.1, and the publication verifier requires the candidate's .github/workflows tree to equal the previous alas tree, so the candidate keeps alas's workflow unchanged. The pin bump is mirrored in a separate level-3 automation/* PR after this sync; it changes no step, input or permission.
